To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a brain injury can be a life changing event for an individual and his or her family, 2) the effects of a brain injury can range from minor to severe and can include physical, cognitive and emotional changes, 3) there is no one way to recover from a brain injury and each individual will have their own unique recovery process.

the following factors are associated with improved outcomes: 1) the use of a multidisciplinary team approach, 2) the use of early intervention, 3) the use of an integrated medical and vocational model, 4) the use of vocational rehabilitation services, and 5) the presence of an on-site employer liaison.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of factors associated with vocational outcomes after brain injury and the development of a comprehensive, integrated hospital-based program for vocational evaluation and rehabilitation.
the development of a new paradigm in rehabilitation medicine that integrates medical and vocational services in the treatment of brain injury and other chronic conditions.
the integration of vocational services into brain injury rehabilitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a significant relationship between brain injury and the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms.
there is no evidence that the use of the CCI in the assessment and management of patients with TBI is superior to the use of other measures of cognitive functioning.
a brain injury rehabilitation team should have a multidisciplinary team approach to the management of the brain injured person.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hospital should be the place for medical and vocational rehabilitation.
a brain injury rehabilitation program that includes medical and vocational services can maximize the vocational outcome for patients with brain injury.
the medical and vocational hospital based rehabilitation services are complementary, and when combined with a strong interdisciplinary team, the outcome is better than either service alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of medical and rehabilitation services in the acute care setting can improve the vocational outcomes for patients with brain injury.
there are no simple answers to questions about the impact of brain injury on employment.
there is a need for better integration of hospital-based medical and vocational services to optimize vocational outcomes.
